A.explanation: In an isolated system total momentum is conserved, so $\Delta p_X = -\Delta p_Y$. The magnitudes of the changes are equal despite $m_X > m_Y$.

B.explanation: By Newton's third law the force of X on Y and of Y on X are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, so neither force is greater.

C.explanation: The contact interaction lasts for one shared time interval, so the force on X and the force on Y start and end together.

D.explanation: A collision involves short-range contact forces due to electromagnetic repulsion between surfaces, not gravitational forces only.

hints: Notice the phrase isolated system and that X and Y collide and then separate, so focus on the pair of forces they exert on each other during contact.
Recall Newton's third law for the two collision forces and conservation of momentum $p = mv$ for the isolated X-Y system.
Compare both the magnitude of $F$ and the contact time $t$ for X on Y versus Y on X, and use impulse $Ft = \Delta p$ to test the statements about momentum change.
walkthrough: Identify the interaction: during the collision X exerts a force $F_{X \text{ on } Y}$ on Y and Y exerts a force $F_{Y \text{ on } X}$ on X.
Apply Newton's third law: these two forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, so $|F_{X \text{ on } Y}| = |F_{Y \text{ on } X}|$ regardless of $m_X > m_Y$.
Consider the time: contact begins and ends at the same instants for both objects, so the interaction time $t$ is common to both forces.
Link to momentum with impulse: $Ft = \Delta p$. Equal $F$ acting for equal $t$ gives equal magnitude impulses, so the momentum changes are equal and opposite.
Therefore the only correct statement is that the mutual forces act for the same length of time. This is option C.
